outcomes.text: Recognise melodic movement, melodic devices, phrases, improvisation, leitmotifs, range, fanfares, hooks, riffs, rāga and quarter-tones.
Identify and understand major, minor, chromatic, modal, pentatonic, rāga and maqām scales or modes.
Recognise duple, triple, quadruple and irregular metres, simple and compound time, syncopation, hemiola, anacrusis, cross-rhythm, polyrhythm and culturally specific rhythmic patterns.
Recognise common Italian tempo markings, tempo changes such as accelerando and rubato, and beats per minute.
Identify major and minor tonality, related-key modulations, and tonic major or minor.
Recognise primary and secondary chords, dominant and diminished sevenths, cadences, types of harmony, suspensions and pedal notes.
Identify monophonic, homophonic, polyphonic, heterophonic, imitative, antiphonal, solo, tutti, drone and other listed textures.
Recognise dynamic levels, crescendos, diminuendos and terraced dynamics.
Identify legato, staccato, accents, sforzando, slurs, trills, mordents, turns, appoggiaturas and acciaccaturas.
Identify orchestral, chamber, keyboard, vocal, popular, salsa, Hindustani, silk-and-bamboo and takht instruments and ensembles.

subtopics.title: Instrumental and vocal techniques, and word-setting

outcomes.text: Recognise instrumental and vocal techniques including pizzicato, glissando, tremolo, double stopping, rolls, melisma, syllabic singing, rap and word-painting.
Identify binary, ternary, rondo, ritornello, sonata form, introduction, cadenza, minuet and trio, theme and variations, and vocal or dance-song structures.
Recognise production techniques and equipment including samples, loops, chorus, reverb, delay, overdubbing, double-tracking, multi-tracking and drum machines.
Read staff notation, clefs, key signatures, rhythmic values, time signatures, common signs, intervals and transposing-instrument parts.
Study Handel’s Concerto Grosso in D major, including movements 4 Largo and 6 Menuet, as examples of Baroque concerto style.
Use the focus works to understand solo concerto and concerto grosso features and typical Baroque performance practice.

outcomes.text: Broaden listening experience through representative Baroque instrumental works, including Bach’s Orchestral Suite and Telemann’s Trio Sonata.
Study Mozart’s Piano and Winds Quintet in E-flat, first movement, as an example of Classical chamber music and sonata form.
Understand the main features of sonata form and the characteristics of Classical instrumental music.

outcomes.text: Study Smetana’s Vltava as an example of Romantic orchestral, programme and national-identity music.
Understand Romantic trends including expanded orchestras, programme music and musical expressions of national identity.

outcomes.text: Explore art song, choral music, popular song and musical theatre from the twentieth century onwards.
Understand how musical features enhance textual meaning and how modern songs use common structures and techniques.

topics.title: Focus areas: Tango; Salsa; EDM (Electronic Dance Music)

subtopics.title: Focus areas: Tango; Salsa; EDM (Electronic Dance Music)

outcomes.text: Recognise the instruments and musical features of tango and salsa, including influences from African and Western music.
Understand the cultural contexts of tango and salsa and how technology and production techniques create EDM.
Identify instruments, style-specific features, social contexts and performance contexts in silk-and-bamboo, Hindustani and Arab takht ensembles.
Understand how orchestral music supports visual action in ballet, film and video games.
Explain how musical features create atmosphere, increase tension or excitement, and enhance particular action moments.
